note: The film, in order. A `card` segment is a still with the narrator over it. A `turn` segment is one question put to the real add-on through the simulated Alexa+: the person's line is `ask`, and the assistant's line is whatever the add-on answers when the frames are captured (video/out/answers.json), never text written here. `group` puts consecutive turns in one voice request. `pause_after` is silence after the segment, in seconds. The film runs close to its three-minute limit: the inhaler question ("I can compare prices for tablets and capsules, but not yet for inhalers") was cut for time.

segments.say: One in five Americans aged sixty-five and over say they didn't take a medicine as prescribed because of its cost. In one study, the insurance copay was higher than the cash price for more than a quarter of generic prescriptions. A pharmacist is allowed to tell you, but only if you ask. Fair Refill is an Alexa Plus add-on for asking.

segments.ask: Am I overpaying for my atorvastatin 20 milligrams? I pay forty dollars a month.

segments.say: Fair Refill is a real MCP server with seven tools, and its card is an MCP App. Every price is for the identical medicine, from a public source, and every answer ends at the pharmacist. Alexa Plus's developer tools weren't open to entrants, so the screen you saw is a stand-in. The add-on behind it is real.
